page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-32GB is a memory-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of x86_64 system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between memory capacity and processing throughput. The shared AMD EPYC processor delivers poor single-core performance in stress-ng tests and weak multi-core performance. Large-block memory bandwidth is also weak, measuring 27.8 GB/sec for read and 19.94 GB/sec for write operations. However, the instance demonstrates average capabilities in text processing, software compilation, and basic decompression tasks. Static web serving throughput is poor, and medium-scale LLM inference is limited.

Given its shared CPU allocation and high memory density, this server type offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require sustained, high-frequency CPU performance. It is suited for caching layers, memory-intensive database operations, text processing pipelines, and lightweight background workers where RAM capacity is the primary constraint rather than raw compute power.
